KEY MESSAGE 1...

In the wake of Saturday night's cold front, we're left with a much 
colder airmass in place locally as surface high pressure builds off 
to our west today. With steepening low level lapse rates in the cold 
advection regime, expect that we'll pop a stratocu deck today and 
mix into some elevated flow around 850 mb providing surface gusts of 
20-30 mph during the daytime hours. A mid-level trough will sweep 
through today and Monday while embedded shortwaves provide weak, 
broad lift supportive of scattered rain and snow showers. One of 
those will pass by this evening and bring a mostly rain or rain/snow 
mix for most outside of the ridges and north of Pittsburgh where 
HREF suggests dominant precipitation type will be snow. 
Thermodynamic profiles from the CAMs show decent lapse rates through 
a saturated DGZ, so while ground temperatures should be marginal to 
support any accumulation, would not be surprised if grass and 
elevated surfaces did see a light coating.

Monday will again feature a diurnal increase in clouds with perhaps 
some very light scattered snow showers as the upper trough axis 
exits. Increasing subsidence as high pressure arrives should 
eventually sink inversion heights below the DGZ and moisture will 
erode thus shutting off the precip. Don't expect wind gusts to be 
near what they were on Sunday with weaker flow aloft and little of a 
gradient beneath the high.

Despite the gradient wind continuing overnight, lows Sunday night 
feature a high probability to dip below 32F north and east of 
Pittsburgh as well as down the PA and WV ridges (60-90+%, highest to 
the north). A Freeze Warning remains in effect for those areas. 
Elsewhere, a Frost Advisory has been issued, but of note with 
that... it's more likely that tonight features a freeze or nothing 
type-scenario with the elevated wind and light precip precluding 
widespread frost development. Only expect that frost will be seen in 
wind-sheltered areas, but given the early season warmth this year, 
and likely some planting already done, the localized threat is worth 
addressing.

Monday night is high probability to feature a widespread freeze 
threat with light wind, lower dew points, and mostly clear skies 
beneath the core of the high supporting excellent radiational 
cooling conditions. Given the recent few weeks' warm overnight lows, 
have shaved a couple degrees off of the NBM mean MinTs which matches 
its probability of 90-100% chance for <32F north of I-70 and 60-80% 
south of I-70. A Freeze Watch has been issued for our entire area 
Monday night, and as to not confuse messaging, advisory/warning 
decisions will come after the expiration of the frost/freeze 
headlines for Sunday night.

KEY MESSAGE 2... 

Albeit with some timing, amplitude, and orientation discrepancy 
among ensembles and AI guidance, mid-level ridging is expected to 
build across the central CONUS and slide east into our area for the 
latter half of the week ultimately providing overall warmer weather 
but with some periods of precipitation chances. We still look to be 
favoring a northwest flow regime on Wednesday as a weak surface low 
dives through Lake Erie to Lake Ontario. This, and an associated 
shortwave, could bring some precip back on Wednesday but amounts 
still look to be light. A drier scenario paints just a few 
hundredths of an inch of rain at best while a deeper mid-level wave, 
favoring the "wet" solution, holds mostly at <0.5" of QPF in a 
scattered nature on the high end. All told, Wednesday does not look 
to feature a notable amount or coverage of rain, and machine 
learning suggests low to zero severe weather probability.

Thursday favors drier and warmer as the ridge axis translates 
overhead and about a 50/50 shot for Pittsburgh reaching 80F (higher 
chance south and west). That period of higher confidence dry weather 
ends quickly as the ridge breaks down Friday into Saturday and 
precip chances likely return. Timing details remain quite uncertain 
owing to discrepancy with the erosion of the ridge as a trough butts 
up against it from the west with arrival time of precip ranging from 
late Friday afternoon to early Saturday morning. Moisture shouldn't 
rebound a whole lot from much lower dew points expected through mid-
week, but, the heat risk map does depict some minor category impacts 
arriving locally for both days. Associated effects would be 
primarily to those who are extremely sensitive to heat without 
relief, so any persons in this category should keep this in mind if 
planning to spend prolonged periods outdoors in the late-week 
timeframe.
